questions.question: Distinguish between luminous and non-luminous objects with two examples of each. Explain why the Moon appears bright although it is non-luminous.
questions.expected_answer: Luminous objects give out their own light, e.g. the Sun, stars, candle flame, bulb, fire, firefly, switched-on screen. Non-luminous objects do not produce light and are seen only by light reflected from them into our eyes, e.g. the Moon, a book, a person, a tree, a mirror. The Moon is a rocky body that reflects sunlight; it appears bright because sunlight falls on it and is reflected towards Earth, and its phases show how much of its sunlit side faces us.

questions.question: Describe an experiment that shows light travels in straight lines. Explain how a pinhole camera forms an image and why the image is inverted.
questions.expected_answer: Make holes in the same position in three cards and stand them in a row between a candle and the eye; when the holes are in a straight line the flame is seen, but moving one card sideways blocks it, because light cannot bend to pass through holes out of line. Pinhole camera: a light-proof box with a tiny hole at one end and a translucent screen at the other. Light from each point on the object travels in a straight line through the pinhole to one point on the screen. Rays from the top of the object travel downwards through the hole and land at the bottom of the screen, and rays from the bottom land at the top, so the image is inverted (and reversed left to right).

questions.question: State the speed of light in a vacuum and calculate the time light takes to travel from the Sun to the Earth (150 000 000 km) and from the Moon to the Earth (384 000 km). Why do we see lightning before we hear thunder?
questions.expected_answer: Speed of light ≈ 300 000 km/s. Sun: t = d ÷ v = 150 000 000 km ÷ 300 000 km/s = 500 s ≈ 8 min 20 s. Moon: t = 384 000 km ÷ 300 000 km/s ≈ 1.3 s. Light travels at about 300 000 km/s while sound travels at about 340 m/s, almost a million times slower, so the light of the flash reaches us almost instantly while the sound of thunder takes about 3 s per kilometre.
